title: I gave my NPCs daily routines. Then I asked Claude for a Monogatari-style edit.
author: Kiko_Production
selftext:
These are the residents of City Paradise, my city builder. Their current achievements include getting off a bus, finding a home, and sitting on a bench. I thought they deserved an introduction.

I've been testing their daily routines: new arrivals explore the town, those who find housing move in, and the rest take the bus back out. Residents visit the available places around town and head home according to their schedule.

The part I care about is being able to follow someone through that day. You see them arrive, spot them somewhere else later, then watch them go home. That's the feeling I'm trying to get working across the town.

The character models need more work, though, and there's a limitation in my current workflow that might be useful to share.

I started with two base models made in Tripo 3D, using GPT and Claude to create visual variations for hairstyles and other details. That gave me different-looking residents, but the resulting models have gaps and holes, especially around the hair. Hats have been particularly troublesome.

So my next experiment is a shared base body with separate heads, hairstyles, and hats, rather than making more variations of complete characters. I'll still be experimenting with Tripo for those parts. Expressions and getting the hair to fit properly will probably take a fair bit of trial and error.

That's the lesson from this batch: getting a varied crowd on screen doesn't mean I've figured out a good way to produce the characters yet.

Also, the edit was made entirely through Claude. I asked for something inspired by Monogatari, and this is what it put together from the test footage.

Has anyone here tried a modular character setup with AI-generated 3D parts? I'd be interested to hear how you handled hair and hats fitting different heads.
